claims.text: High-entropy alloys can be used to produce a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
The proposed transition arises from the high-entropy, severe-lattice-distortion, sluggish-diffusion, and cocktail effects.
(CoNi)50(TiZrHf)50 is a single-phase high-entropy intermetallic alloy.
(CoNi)50(TiZrHf)50 has a face-centered-cubic structure.
Reducing Al content is a viable compositional intervention in Al-containing refractory HEAs.
Reducing Al content controls the order–disorder transformation temperature and limits long-range ordering during solidification.

The proposed testing includes compression from room temperature to about 0.9Tm at 1 × 10−3 s−1, microcompression of 1 μm pillars at room temperature, 573 K, and 673 K, and in situ STEM at room temperature and 573 K.
Atomic-size and electronic-property misfit causes severe lattice distortion.
Severe lattice distortion mitigates differences in atomic bonding among crystallographic orientations.
The altered orientation dependence enables multiple dislocation modes and isotropic mechanical behavior.
Dislocation glide disturbs local chemical order.
Disruption of local chemical order creates structural instability and amorphization at low temperatures.
At high temperatures, local crystal-like order forms and produces dynamic hardening.
Dynamic hardening impedes subsequent dislocation glide and stabilizes plastic flow.
The HEA will exhibit a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
The (CoNi)50(TiZrHf)50 alloy can exhibit high strength and substantial plasticity at room temperature and retain favorable mechanical behavior at high homologous temperatures.
The predicted mechanical behavior is caused by the combination of lattice distortion, dislocation multiplicity, and dynamic hardening.
Conventional intermetallics are typically brittle because of strong long-range order and limited dislocation mobility.
The boundaries between ductile and brittle regimes depend on alloy composition, processing, and test conditions.
The exact mechanisms of hydrogen embrittlement and of defect-mediated hydrogen transport and accumulation in HEAs remain uncertain.

contradictions.description: The material is identified as FCC, but the cited source from which the stated test conditions are taken identifies the same (CoNi)50(TiZrHf)50 alloy as an ordered B2 alloy rather than FCC.

The initial material is the Co-Ni-Ti-Zr-Hf alloy, whereas the intervention of reducing Al refers to distinct Al-Hf-Nb-Ti-V refractory alloys; the hypothesis does not define a single composition to which both fields apply.
